what_worked: Clean, consistent visual template with readable typography and clear slide hierarchy.
fix_next: This is a fictional investor pitch, not a data-story; nearly every quantitative claim is fabricated or unsupported by the dataset.
verdict: Generic AI-generated pitch deck with fabricated metrics; not a data analysis.
factual_error_detail: S3: Claims '$30M aggregate MRR'—actual total 30-day revenue is ~$15.6M. Claims 'CAC, churn retention' benchmarks exist in dataset—they do not. S4: 'Average MRR $4,682'—not verifiable as stated; revenue share tiers (85%, 55%, 35%, 18%) appear fabricated and don't sum logically (cumulative? overlapping?). Top-10 share is 49.6%, not 85%. S5: 'MRR Growth Velocity' chart is entirely fabricated—dataset is a cross-sectional snapshot, no time-series data exists. '3.4x faster payback period' is invented. S7: 'Dataset Industry Average' column ($420 CAC, 2.2x LTV:CAC, 72% gross margin, 94% NRR) are all fabricated—none of these metrics exist in the dataset. S2: '60% of potential LTV left on the table' is unsupported. S1: '31 SaaS categories'—dataset has ~12 named categories with 274 missing.

evidence.insight: No genuine insight derived from the dataset. Slides 4-5 present fabricated tiering and growth curves rather than actual findings about category revenue, provider distribution, or audience-type patterns.
evidence.narrative: Follows a standard investor pitch template (opportunity → data → product → unit economics → projections → ask) but this is the wrong genre for a data-story assignment. No analytical thesis is developed or tested.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 frames as 'investor pitch' rather than data analysis. No mention of missingness (274 category, 241 country, 288 audience_type missing). No limitations discussed. Audience and question are misaligned with assignment.
evidence.accuracy: Virtually every number is either fabricated or wrong. $30M total (actual ~$15.6M). Revenue tier shares don't match dataset. CAC/LTV/NRR/gross margin metrics don't exist in the data. Growth velocity chart has no basis. '31 categories' is wrong.
evidence.visual: Template is clean and professional with consistent blue palette, good whitespace, and readable fonts. But charts on slides 4-5 are decorative fabrications, and slide 7's table presents invented benchmarks as data-derived.
evidence.ai_slop: Pervasive. Consulting buzzwords throughout ('workflow-first SaaS platform with automated acquisition loops,' 'defensible stickiness,' 'top-quartile velocity'). Slide 6 is pure product marketing filler. Slide 9 is a generic roadmap. Slide 10 is a boilerplate VC ask. The entire deck reads as an AI-generated pitch template with dataset name inserted.
